# everpure_azure_snapshot (Resource)

Manages a manual Volume Group Snapshot: a point-in-time snapshot of every volume in a Volume Group.

A snapshot is immutable once created, and snapshots taken by this resource are never expired by the volume group's snapshot schedule: each one stays until it is destroyed.

~> **Destroying the parent volume group soft-deletes this snapshot with it.** The backend destroys every snapshot in a volume group as part of destroying the group itself, and eradicating the group eradicates its snapshots. See [Deletion policies](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure/latest/docs/guides/deletion-policies).

To read a snapshot managed elsewhere, including one taken by the volume group's snapshot schedule, use the [`everpure_azure_snapshot` data source](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure/latest/docs/data-sources/snapshot). A snapshot taken by the schedule cannot be managed by this resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    everpure = {
      source = "PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure"
    }
  }
}

provider "everpure" {
  subscription_id = var.subscription_id
}

variable "subscription_id" {
  type = string
}

variable "storage_pool_id" {
  type        = string
  description = "Full ARM ID of an existing Everpure Storage Pool in the same subscription."
}

data "everpure_azure_volume_group" "example" {
  name            = "vg-prod-east"
  storage_pool_id = var.storage_pool_id
}

# A snapshot of every volume in the volume group. It has no updatable
# attributes: changing the name or volume group creates a new snapshot. It stays
# until it is destroyed.
resource "everpure_azure_snapshot" "example" {
  name            = "snap-before-upgrade"
  volume_group_id = data.everpure_azure_volume_group.example.id

  # Overrides the defaults, which normally protect a snapshot from destroy.
  deletion_protection  = false # true (default) blocks destroy + replace
  eradicate_on_destroy = true  # false (default) soft-deletes, recoverable
}

# A volume restored from the snapshot above. volume_name is the name the source
# volume had when the snapshot was taken, as reported in volume_snapshots.
resource "everpure_azure_volume" "restored" {
  name            = "vol-prod-data-restored"
  volume_group_id = data.everpure_azure_volume_group.example.id
  source_type     = "snapshot"

  source_snapshot {
    id          = everpure_azure_snapshot.example.id
    volume_name = everpure_azure_snapshot.example.volume_snapshots[0].volume_name
  }
}

# A whole volume group restored from the snapshot.
resource "everpure_azure_volume_group" "restored" {
  name               = "vg-prod-east-restored"
  storage_pool_id    = var.storage_pool_id
  source_type        = "snapshot"
  source_snapshot_id = everpure_azure_snapshot.example.id
}

# A snapshot recovered after it was soft-deleted. The source must be in the same
# volume group, and must not have been taken by the snapshot schedule. Recovering
# restores that snapshot under the name given here; it does not copy it.
resource "everpure_azure_snapshot" "recovered" {
  name                           = "snap-before-upgrade-recovered"
  volume_group_id                = data.everpure_azure_volume_group.example.id
  source_recoverable_snapshot_id = "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-storage-prod/providers/PureStorage.Block/storagePools/pool-prod-east/volumeGroups/vg-prod-east/snapshots/snap-deleted-20260827141136"
}

output "snapshot_id" {
  value = everpure_azure_snapshot.example.id
}

output "snapshot_created_at" {
  value = everpure_azure_snapshot.example.created_at
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the snapshot. The name must be 2-40 characters, start with a letter, end with a letter or digit, and contain only letters, numbers and hyphens. Changing this forces a new snapshot to be created.
- `volume_group_id` (String) Full Azure Resource Manager ID of the volume group to snapshot. Changing this forces a new snapshot to be created.

### Optional

- `deletion_protection` (Boolean) Whether to block destroying this snapshot, or replacing it (which destroys it as part of the replacement). Defaults to `true`. Set to `false`, and apply, before a destroy or a change that would otherwise force replacement.
- `eradicate_on_destroy` (Boolean) Whether destroy permanently eradicates the snapshot instead of soft-deleting it. Defaults to `false`. There is no recovery window once eradicated.
- `source_recoverable_snapshot_id` (String) Full Azure Resource Manager ID of a soft-deleted snapshot to recover instead of taking a new one. The snapshot is restored (not copied) under `name` and must be in the same volume group. Snapshots taken by the snapshot schedule can't be recovered through this resource. Changing this forces a new snapshot to be created. Imported snapshots always have it unset.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the snapshot was created, as an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC. Timestamps sort chronologically as strings.
- `id` (String) The full Azure Resource Manager ID of the snapshot, e.g. `/subscriptions/.../resourceGroups/.../providers/PureStorage.Block/storagePools/pool1/volumeGroups/vg1/snapshots/snap1`.
- `volume_snapshots` (Attributes List) The snapshot of each volume in the volume group at the time the snapshot was taken. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--volume_snapshots))

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) Defaults to 20 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when creating the snapshot.
- `delete` (String) Defaults to 35 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when destroying the snapshot, including eradicating its recoverable copy when eradicate_on_destroy is set.
- `read` (String) Defaults to 5 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when reading the snapshot.


<a id="nestedatt--volume_snapshots"></a>
### Nested Schema for `volume_snapshots`

Read-Only:

- `provisioned_size_in_bytes` (Number) Provisioned size of the source volume, in bytes.
- `serial_number` (String) Serial number of the source volume, as recorded when the snapshot was taken.
- `volume_name` (String) Name of the source volume when the snapshot was taken. This is the value for `source_snapshot.volume_name` on an `everpure_azure_volume` restoring from this snapshot.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = everpure_azure_snapshot.example
  identity = {
    subscription_id     = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
    resource_group_name = "rg-storage-prod"
    storage_pool_name   = "pool-prod-east"
    volume_group_name   = "vg-prod-east"
    name                = "snap-before-upgrade"
  }
}

resource "everpure_azure_snapshot" "example" {
  # ... configuration matching the imported snapshot
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the snapshot.
- `resource_group_name` (String) Name of the resource group the resource lives in.
- `storage_pool_name` (String) Name of the storage pool the snapshot belongs to.
- `subscription_id` (String) Azure subscription ID the resource lives in.
- `volume_group_name` (String) Name of the volume group the snapshot belongs to.

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Snapshots are imported by their full Azure resource ID. A snapshot taken by the
# volume group's snapshot schedule cannot be imported; read it with the
# everpure_azure_snapshot data source instead.
terraform import everpure_azure_snapshot.example \
  "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-storage-prod/providers/PureStorage.Block/storagePools/pool-prod-east/volumeGroups/vg-prod-east/snapshots/snap-before-upgrade"
```
